## The Cosmological Collider

<img src="/assets/img/research_cosmo_collider.png" alt="Cosmological collider signal in the galaxy bispectrum" style="float: right; margin: 0 0 1em 1.5em; width: 260px; border-radius: 4px; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.15);">

I search for signatures of massive particles produced during cosmic inflation -- the "cosmological collider" program. Using both galaxy survey data (BOSS power spectrum and bispectrum) and CMB higher-point functions, I constrain the masses and spins of particles present during inflation, opening a unique observational window into ultra-high-energy particle physics. My recent work extends these searches to the cosmic microwave background and critically assesses how well collider signatures can actually be measured from current data.

Key papers: [Philcox 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18369), [Philcox 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12010), [Cabass, Philcox, Ivanov et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01894)

## CMB Higher-Point Functions

<img src="/assets/img/research_cmb_hpf.png" alt="CMB bispectrum constraint results" style="float: right; margin: 0 0 1em 1.5em; width: 260px; border-radius: 4px; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.15);">

I build efficient optimal estimators for the CMB bispectrum and trispectrum on the full sky, applicable to both scalar and tensor perturbations. I have used these to place the first constraints on the primordial trispectrum from Planck data, to search for tensor and mixed tensor-scalar non-Gaussianity, and to constrain arbitrary primordial bispectrum shapes without assuming a fixed template.

Key papers: [Philcox 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17004), [Philcox, Zhong & Sirletti 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.19179), [Philcox 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.04434)

<div style="clear: both;"></div>

## Galaxy Power Spectrum and Bispectrum Analysis

<img src="/assets/img/research_galaxy_ps.png" alt="Galaxy power spectrum and bispectrum measurements" style="float: right; margin: 0 0 1em 1.5em; width: 260px; border-radius: 4px; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.15);">

I develop optimal, window-free estimators for measuring galaxy clustering statistics and apply them to state-of-the-art survey data. My recent work includes joint power spectrum and bispectrum analyses of BOSS and DESI DR1 data within perturbation theory -- now extended to two-loop order -- yielding precise constraints on cosmological parameters including the Hubble constant, neutrino masses, dark energy, and primordial non-Gaussianity.

Key papers: [Philcox 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13867), [Ivanov, Sullivan, de Belsunce et al. 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.16165), [Chudaykin, Ivanov & Philcox 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.13433)

<div style="clear: both;"></div>

## Inflation from Galaxy Surveys

<img src="/assets/img/research_inflation.png" alt="Primordial non-Gaussianity constraints from DESI galaxies" style="float: right; margin: 0 0 1em 1.5em; width: 260px; border-radius: 4px; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.15);">

I use the galaxy bispectrum from BOSS and DESI data -- analyzed within the framework of the effective field theory of large-scale structure -- to constrain models of single-field and multifield inflation, including searches for equilateral, folded, and oscillatory primordial signals. This work provides some of the tightest constraints on primordial non-Gaussianity parameters from galaxy clustering.

Key papers: [Chen, Chudaykin, Ivanov et al. 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10530), [Yang & Philcox 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15337), [Chudaykin, Ivanov & Philcox 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.04266)

<div style="clear: both;"></div>

## Parity Violation in Cosmology

<img src="/assets/img/research_parity.png" alt="Parity-odd trispectrum measurements from CMB data" style="float: right; margin: 0 0 1em 1.5em; width: 260px; border-radius: 4px; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.15);">

I conduct systematic searches for parity-violating signatures in both galaxy surveys and the CMB. This includes the first measurement of the parity-odd four-point correlation function from BOSS galaxies, a careful assessment of whether that signal could arise from sample variance, and tests of parity using CMB temperature and polarization bispectra.

Key papers: [Philcox & Ereza 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.09523), [Philcox & Shiraishi 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.03831), [Philcox 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04227)

<div style="clear: both;"></div>

## The Hubble Constant and Dark Energy

<img src="/assets/img/research_hubble.png" alt="Modified Hubble expansion rate from topological boundaries" style="float: right; margin: 0 0 1em 1.5em; width: 260px; border-radius: 4px; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.15);">

I have pioneered sound-horizon-independent measurements of the Hubble constant using the matter-radiation equality scale from galaxy surveys, CMB lensing, and supernovae. More recently, I have used full-shape galaxy clustering analyses of DESI data to constrain dark energy, spatial curvature, and neutrino masses, and to test beyond-LCDM physics.

Key papers: [Smith, Ivanov, de Belsunce et al. 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10794), [Chudaykin, Ivanov & Philcox 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.20757), [Philcox, Silverstein & Torroba 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.00115)

<div style="clear: both;"></div>

## Simulation-Based Inference

<img src="/assets/img/research_sbi.png" alt="Hybrid simulation-based inference posterior comparison" style="float: right; margin: 0 0 1em 1.5em; width: 260px; border-radius: 4px; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.15);">

I develop hybrid simulation-based inference methods that combine analytic likelihoods with neural network emulators, enabling more robust cosmological analyses that go beyond traditional summary statistics -- including the simulation-based priors now used in state-of-the-art DESI full-shape analyses.

Key papers: [Jacobus, Tucci & Philcox 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27320), [Chudaykin, Ivanov & Philcox 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.18554), [Zhang, Modi & Philcox 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.13591)
